Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

CHAPTER II
GENDER MAINSTREAMING (PUG)
Part One
Policy on the Implementation of PUG

Article 20
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 18 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 21
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 18 letters c and d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 5
(1) Regional Governments formulate Gender Responsive development policies, programs, and activities as set forth in:
a. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD);
b. SKPD Strategic Plan; and
c. SKPD Work Plan.
(2) The formulation of Gender Responsive development policies, programs, and activities as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through Gender Analysis.

Third Part
Programs and Activities for the Protection of Women and Children

CHAPTER VI
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 33
(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. provision of guidelines and fulfillment of Minimum Service Standards for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Further provisions regarding guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25. Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for Regional Governments in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 35. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Third Part
Scope

Article 27
(1) P2TP2A has the principal task of implementing part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services in a fast, precise and integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and to Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and human trafficking.
(2) In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the following functions:
a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which are emergency in nature in a fast manner covering various services namely information, medical referral, legal, psychological, mental, safe house (shelter), home visit and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building work networks that synergize with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims post-handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Paragraph 1
P2TP2A
Article 26
(1) In order to provide protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center in implementing programs and activities for the protection of women and children.
(2) The establishment, organization, and work procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 29
(1) The Task Force as referred to in Article 28 letter a, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, Law Enforcement, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Professional Organizations, and Researchers/Academics.
(2) The Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution that has the duty to coordinate programs and activities for the prevention and handling of victims of violence against Women and Children, as well as Trafficking in Persons.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organization, duties and functions of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 28
In addition to establishing P2TP2A as referred to in Article 26, in order to support the implementation of protection for women and children, the Regent shall establish:
a. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Victims of Violence Against Women, Victims of Violence Against Children, and Trafficking in Persons;
b. Regional Action Committee for the Elimination of the Worst Forms of Child Labor.

CHAPTER IV
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part One
Obligations and Responsibilities

Article 34
The guidance and supervision as referred to in Article 33, shall be implemented in order to realize the objectives of the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in accordance with the minimum service standards established by the Government.

4.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 9 ayat (2) huruf c explicitly assigns the PUG Focal Point to conduct “pelatihan, sosialisasi, advokasi Pengarusutamaan Gender kepada seluruh pejabat dan staf di lingkungan SKPD” (training/socialization/advocacy of gender mainstreaming to all officials/staff). This is clearly an education/awareness activity about gender equality (PUG is defined in Pasal 1 angka 8 as a strategy integrating gender into planning/implementation/monitoring/evaluation). Therefore the policy does contain gender-equality-related education/awareness measures, so a “Yes” is supportable from the ground-truth text; the golden “No” appears incorrect.

5.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text Pasal 32 ayat (3) states the Gugus Tugas KLA membership “dapat melibatkan Instansi terkait, dunia usaha, tokoh agama/masyarakat/adat, dan masyarakat.” The explicit inclusion of “tokoh … adat” (customary/traditional leaders) is direct evidence of engaging traditional/cultural leadership structures. Thus the judge’s “Yes” matches the ground truth; the golden label “No” appears wrong.

5.6.evaluator_rationale: While the definition of community institutions lists mass media as a type of organization, the provided sentences do not show the policy engaging or assigning any role to media in prevention, protection, or services.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is West Bandung Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration. 3. Regent is the Regent of West Bandung. 4. Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning, hereinafter abbreviated as BP3AKB is a regional apparatus that has the main duties, functions, and affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning in the Region. 5. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to strengthen women's basic rights, improve quality of life, and increase women's participation in development. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region. 9. Improvement of Women's Quality of Life hereinafter abbreviated as PKHP is an effort to improve the physical and mental conditions of women in fulfilling their rights and life needs as part of human rights from various fields of development, especially education, health, economy, science and technology (IPTEK), socio-culture, politics, law and the environment. 10. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and women in respect of their rights so they can live, grow, participate, be free from all forms of violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection against trafficking of children and women. 11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 12. Gender Analysis is an analysis to identify and understand the division of work/roles of men and women, access and control over development resources, participation in the development process, and the benefits they enjoy, the pattern of unequal relationships between men and women, which in its implementation takes into account other factors such as social class, race, and ethnicity. 13. Gender Responsive Budget is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 14. Gender Budget Statement hereinafter abbreviated as GBS is a document that informs that an activity output has been gender responsive to existing gender issues, and/or a cost has been allocated to the activity output to address gender gap problems. 15. Focal Point PUG is SKPD apparatus who have the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 16. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 17. Toddler Family Development hereinafter referred to as BKB is a community movement directed to increase the knowledge and skills of parents in fostering the growth and development of children aged 0-5 years. 18. Love Mother Movement hereinafter referred to as GSI is a movement carried out by the community and government to improve the quality of life of women through various activities that have an impact on efforts to accelerate the reduction of maternal mortality rates (AKI) due to pregnancy, childbirth and postpartum as well as the reduction of infant mortality rates (AKB). 19. Model Village of Advanced Independent Indonesian Women hereinafter referred to as Model Village PRIMA is a pilot village to overcome poverty through economic efforts accompanied by reduction of health and education cost burdens for poor families, by utilizing all potential/resources both natural and human. 20. Improvement of Women's Role Towards Healthy and Prosperous Families hereinafter referred to as P2WKSS is an integrated program for increasing the role of women that uses a cross-sectoral development approach in a coordinated manner to improve family quality. 21. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, integrated crisis centers (PKT), integrated service centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, science and technology information centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms. 22. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons is a forum for cross-sectoral collaboration and coordination that aims to guarantee the implementation of prevention and handling of criminal acts of trafficking in persons, especially women and children in the Region. 23. Community institution is an institution formed by members of Indonesian citizen society voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations. 24.

Article 20
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 18 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 29
(1) The Task Force as referred to in Article 28 letter a, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, Law Enforcement, Community Organizations, Non-Governmental Organizations, Professional Organizations, and Researchers/Academics.
(2) The Task Force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative institution that has the duty to coordinate programs and activities for the prevention and handling of victims of violence against Women and Children, as well as Trafficking in Persons.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organization, duties and functions of the Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 25
(1) The form of service as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be implemented by the Regional Government in accordance with minimum service standards established by the Government.
(2) In the implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may cooperate with government agencies, provincial governments, other district/city governments, law enforcement officials, and the community.
(3) Further provisions regarding procedures for service and handling of women and children victims of acts of violence as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25. Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for Regional Governments in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions normally. 35. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

5.6.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 1 angka 23 defines “Lembaga masyarakat” and explicitly lists “media massa” (mass media) as one of the forms of community institutions (“… organisasi politik, media massa, dan bentuk organisasi lainnya”). This is an explicit recognition of media as a stakeholder category within the policy’s implementation ecosystem. Given the indicator is “Media engagement,” this definition provides at least a policy-level inclusion/engagement hook for media. The judge rejected it as merely definitional, but the golden label is “Yes,” and the ground-truth text supports that “Yes” at least to the extent of formally including mass media among participating institutions; therefore the predicted “No” is inconsistent with the document and the golden label seems more plausible than the judge’s strict interpretation.
